sections.h2: Where is the Platte County, MO Recorder of Deeds office?
sections.html:
The office is in the Platte County Administration Building at 415 Third St., Room 035, Platte City, MO 64079. Call (816) 858-3326. Christopher L. Wright, who won the seat in November 2022, also lists (816) 858-1832 as his number.

The counter keeps two sets of hours. Anyone searching records or buying copies can walk in between 8 a.m. and 5 p.m., lunch hour included. New documents are accepted for recording only from 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. The county's remaining closures for 2026 fall on Thursday and Friday, November 26 and 27, and on December 24 and 25.

sections.h2: What does the Platte County recorder do in a home sale?
sections.html:
The recorder keeps the county's permanent land records. The office lists its work as recording real estate transactions, filing state and federal tax liens, holding military discharge papers and issuing marriage licenses. When a Platte County house sells, the deed to the buyer is recorded here, and so is the release that a lender files after its loan is paid off.

Uniform Commercial Code filings are not part of this office's work, because the Missouri Secretary of State has taken them since July 1, 2001. Only the DD214 disclaimer form needs a formal request. For other documents, you can phone or email and staff will pull them without a Sunshine request.

The custodian of records, Travis Youmans, takes any formal request at extension 3326 of the main number. The county notes that real estate and marriage records are public, while divorce records sit with the Circuit Clerk. Marriage license applications are taken from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m.

sections.h2: What are the recording fees at the Platte County recorder?
sections.html:
Expect $26 for the first page and $3 for every page after it when the document meets the standards. A statewide fee increase took effect on August 28, 2026, and the county says it touched recorded documents, marriage licenses and plats. That date is behind us, so the schedule below is the one in use. The fee page adds that overpayments are not refunded, which makes a phone call for the exact total worth the time.

Platte County recorder charges on the county fee page
ItemFee
Standard real estate document, first page$26.00
Each page after the first$3.00
Non-standard document, first page$51.00
Plat or survey, first page$71.00
Plat or survey, each added page$50.00
Recorded document copy, per page$1.00
Certification of a copy$1.00

A document that releases or assigns more than one item adds $5 for each extra item. The county site also lists a $53 marriage license fee, charged in exact cash or by card with a convenience fee. Source: Platte County Recorder Fees.

sections.h2: What turns a Platte County deed into a non-standard document?
sections.html:
Missing the Recorders Association of Missouri layout rules adds a $25 charge, which is exactly the gap between $26 and $51 on the first page. The rules date from January 1, 2002, and a title company or attorney will normally have them built into the deed form. A seller drafting a deed alone should check each item.

  • Letter-size paper that is white or light, 20-pound, without logos or watermarks.
  • Dark ink on one side, with type of at least 8 points.
  • The top 3 inches of page one left empty for the recorder's stamp, and three-quarter inch margins elsewhere.
  • A typed, stamped or printed name under every signature.
  • No tape or staples holding attachments to a page, other than a secure bar-coded label.

Page one must show the title, the date, each grantor with marital status, each grantee, statutory addresses and the legal description, and the words grantor and grantee must appear so the instrument can be indexed. A street address is not accepted as a legal description. See the county formatting page.

sections.h2: Which Platte County documents skip the formatting rules?
sections.html:
Several kinds of paper are exempt and pay only the per-page fee. Documents signed before January 1, 2002 are one group. The others are military separation papers, documents signed outside the United States, certified copies, judgments or papers shaped to court rules, and fixture filings on national approved forms. A document is also exempt when one of the original parties has died or is incapacitated.

Any cover sheet is optional, but if one is used it is recorded as page one and must have the 3-inch top margin and the first-page information. A paper sent in for re-recording needs a new first page or cover sheet that meets the same rules. Rejected documents come back with a reason stated.

sections.h2: Can I search or get alerts on Platte County records online?
sections.html:
Yes. The recorder's iRecord portal at plattemo.icounty.com handles searches, and the same site runs a free Record Notification Service. You register for a free account, confirm the email link, choose your criteria, and the system sends a message whenever a matching deed is recorded.

An owner can set the alert on their own name. The county adds that its data is not official and does not replace advice from a licensed professional. Online search pricing belongs to the portal, so ask the office or read the site before relying on any number.

sections.h2: Does a Platte County deed trigger a transfer tax?
sections.html:
The recorder's published schedule lists recording, copy and plat charges and has no line for a transfer tax. For tax advice on a sale, a title company or Missouri attorney is the right call, and the recorder at (816) 858-3326 can tell you what the office itself collects when it accepts a deed.

Property tax is a separate matter. The Platte County Collector bills it, with statements due on receipt and delinquent after December 31. The Assessor's office also lists a sales validation and education coordinator at (816) 858-1256, which is a useful number when a sale price needs to be explained to the county.

sections.h2: How busy is the Platte County recording market?
sections.html:
Platte County is part of the Kansas City metro area and is far larger than Pike County and Polk County. Census QuickFacts counts 114,400 residents and 47,969 housing units for July 1, 2025. A typical owned home is worth $345,100, owners occupy 67.4 percent of homes and 425 building permits were issued in 2025.

The county was organized on December 31, 1838, and the courthouse at Platte City carries a National Register listing. The recorder's staff includes a chief of staff, an assistant chief deputy and two deputy recorders, and a transparency portal posts the office's receipts. Because new documents are accepted only until 4 p.m., send a deed early in the day. Source: Census QuickFacts.

faqs.q: What does the first page of a standard deed cost in Platte County?
faqs.a: It costs $26.00, and every added page costs $3.00. A document that misses the formatting standards costs $51.00 for the first page.

faqs.q: When can I file a document with the Platte County recorder?
faqs.a: Bring it between 9 a.m. and 4 p.m. on a weekday. The office stays open from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. for searches and copies.

faqs.q: What address do I use to send a deed for recording in Platte County?
faqs.a: Use the Recorder of Deeds, 415 Third St., Room 035, Platte City, MO 64079. Call (816) 858-3326 to confirm the total, because overpayments are not refunded.

faqs.q: How can I be told when a deed is recorded in Platte County?
faqs.a: Register for a free account at plattemo.icounty.com and set your criteria in the Record Notification Service. The system emails you when a matching deed reaches the office.

faqs.q: Does the Platte County recorder file UCC statements?
faqs.a: No. The Missouri Secretary of State has taken UCC filings since July 1, 2001. A real estate fixture filing on the approved form with the required addendum is priced at $26.00 for the first page.
